items.title: Adding mypy type checking to finn.util scripts
items.body:
# Overview

This PR begins addressing issue #1146 by adding mypy config settings, pre-commit settings, and type annotations. Starting with just scripts in /src/finn/utils/ for now, since this is a lot of work (and a lot of potential checking by reviewers) I'm thinking tackling this in stages will be best. For now, config is set to only look at utils/ and ignore all else for mypy checks.

# Motivation

Copied and pasted from the Issue: 

Personally I found that when developing in FINN, it was immensely helpful to have type hints added. This makes the projects structure very clear and helps especially newcomers to understand how components play together much quicker. Additionally, when having long iteration cycles due to for example synthesis times, having a static type checker such as mypy can prevent some of the errors before the run has even started, potentially saving quite some time.

# Workflow

What I've done here for each file is:
- Select a target file to fix.
- Run e.g. `mypy --strict src/finn/util/config.py` to see issues.
- Run a search to see where these functions are called to verify proper annotations to use.
- Make fixes so that mypy --strict passes.

At the end, ran pre-commit to verify it handles mypy correctly.

Note: mypy is added to requirements.txt but this is only really necessary for devs, as pre-commit runs it's own VM with a mirror of mypy in it. It runs ignoring missing args (and not strict) for all files. This can be changed in the future adding the following to .pre-commit-config.yaml:
```
    hooks:
    -   id: mypy
        args: [--strict, --ignore-missing-imports]
```
but I think it is okay to leave out for now mid-migration, so nothing is broken.

# Migration Plan

mypy.ini allows existing code to pass without checking, only the utils/ scripts are checked for now. This file will continue to be updated as needed as mypy types are added. My goal if this PR is accepted/merged is to continue this process.

items.title: Fixing verbose logging error at verbose=3 for reference_evaluator
items.body:
### Description

When `a` is a zero-size numpy array, calling `.min()` and `.max()` throws `ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity`.

Fix was to add empty array check (but only where error occurs) to `reference_evaluator.py` using standard numpy method `a.size == 0` where `verbose < 4`. Performance friendly, does not need to convert the array to python objects first.

Added a test function to `reference_evaluator_test.py` to test the cases (empty arrays) that caused the bug. Verifies output shape/content and that it doesn't crash. Testing verbosity levels 2, 3, 4, and 15 like other tests e.g. `test_reference_evaluator_no_attribute_verbose` do.

### Motivation and Context

Fixes #4860

items.title: Fix index out of bounds in version converter adapters

labels.name: module: version converter
labels.description: Issues related to ONNX version converter

items.body:
### Description
Several version converter adapters were accessing optional inputs without bounds checking, potentially causing index oob errors when those inputs were not provided. Added size checks before accessing inputs[1] in split, reshape, resize, scatter, and axes conversion adapters. Also added relevant tests

### Motivation and Context
Fixes #4874

items.title: Fix FOG shader issue in Compatibility mode
items.body:
Removing `#ifndef DISABLE_FOG` from two places to fix shader issues in Compatibility mode. Additionally, removing `if (scene_data.fog_enabled)` from the same, as the shader will not function properly in compatibility mode otherwise. Manually setting `fog_enabled` to `true` breaks the shader in a different way, implying that `fog_enabled` should not need to be `true` for this shader to function in compatibility mode.

- Fixes #94183
